title: JavaScript Tutorial
description: Master JavaScript step-by-step, from setup to modern ES6+ features. Includes interactive code challenges and practical examples for each topic.

content.content: Setup JavaScript
JavaScript can run directly in the browser console or inside an HTML file.

content: Open your browser and press F12 → Console tab
Write JavaScript code directly in the console
Or, include `<script>` tags in an HTML file and run it

content.content: Execute JavaScript Syntax
JavaScript syntax can be executed directly in the browser or with Node.js.
console.log("Hello, World!");

questions.question: Write a JavaScript program to print 'Hello, JavaScript!'

content.content: Comments in JavaScript
Comments can be single-line `//` or multi-line `/* ... */`.

// This is a comment
console.log("Hello");

questions.question: Write a comment saying 'My first JS program' and print Hello

content.content: Creating Variables
Variables can be declared using `let`, `const`, or `var`.

questions.question: Create a variable age with value 25 and print it

content.content: Data Types in JavaScript
JavaScript has data types like number, string, boolean, object, array, null, undefined, and symbol.

let x = 5;       // number
let y = 3.14;    // number
let z = "Hello"; // string

questions.question: Create variables of number, string, and boolean type and print each

content.content: Number Types
JavaScript uses `number` type for both integers and floating-point numbers.

let a = 10;    // integer
let b = 5.5;   // float
let c = 2e5;   // exponential

questions.question: Assign a floating number 7.25 to a variable and print it

content.content: Type Conversion
Casting can be done with functions like Number(), String(), and Boolean().

questions.question: Convert string '42' to a number and print it

content.content: Working with Strings
Strings are written inside quotes and have many built-in methods.

questions.question: Store 'JavaScript' in a variable and print the first 4 letters

content.content: Boolean Values
Booleans represent logical values: true or false.

questions.question: Write an expression that returns true if 15 is greater than 7

content.content: Operators in JavaScript
Operators perform operations on variables and values: +, -, *, /, %, etc.
Arrays
Arrays are used to store multiple values in one variable.

let fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"];
console.log(fruits[0]);

questions.question: Create an array of 3 numbers and print the last number

content.content: Objects
Objects are collections of key-value pairs.

let person = {name: "John", age: 30};
console.log(person.name);

questions.question: Create an object with name and age, print age

content.content: If...Else Statements
JavaScript supports if, else if, and else conditions.

questions.question: Write an if statement that prints 'Yes' if 8 is less than 10

content.content: Switch Statement
Switch is used to perform different actions based on different conditions.

questions.question: Write a switch statement that prints 'Three' if variable is 3
